parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Part 4. You will hear a lecture about the symbiotic relationship between humans and a bird called the greater honeyguide.

First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.

The greater honeyguide bird is a fascinating creature. I've spent the last eight years studying the species in southern Africa with the Yao community in the Niassa Reserve in Mozambique. The birds do help local hunters find wild beehives. The male bird is recognizable by its pink beak, black throat, and yellow shoulder patch. The female has a black beak and a duller color, while the young birds have a distinctive yellow throat and a noticeable ring around the eye. The collaborative arrangement between hunters and greater honeyguides was first documented as early as 1588. But only in our most recent study have we realized the extent to which birds and humans communicate. The reason this relationship has developed is because the trees in the Niassa Reserve, therefore, the hives are especially high, sometimes up to 30 meters, which makes them very hard to find. The birds locate the beehives stashed away in holes in trees, which the hunters then access in order to make off with the pure, sticky honey inside. But they also leave something behind for the greater honeyguides. They are among the few bird species that can eat and digest wax in this way. The interaction between humans and birds benefits both parties. The relationship between the greater honeyguide and the hunters in Mozambique remains very strong. The Yao community considers their communication with the greater honeyguide to be part of their identity. But in some countries outside Mozambique, villagers are now turning more to farming and keeping their own hives, which has led to the role of the bird in honey collection growing smaller. The phenomenon of the greater honeyguides and the honey hunters is really quite remarkable. This level of complex communication is otherwise unheard of in nature. In fact, what we found with these greater honeyguides is the only known example of targeted two-way communication between people and a free-living species. The most remarkable thing about this relationship is the signals people use to communicate with the greater honeyguides. But how do the birds learn to work with people? Well, we believe the behavior is innate. The birds inherit the knowledge and then refine it to match their region as they grow. In different parts of the world, they learn to respond to different sounds made by humans. When the Yao people are ready to hunt, they make a specific noise by unrolling their tongues in a particular way to let the greater honeyguides know. In Tanzania, on the other hand, greater honeyguides listen for a whistle as a sign to begin hunting. While in Zambia, the sound of chopping wood is the cue. The methods used for gathering honey in the Niassa Reserve are actually no different from those used by most beekeepers around the world. In order to relax the bees and make the process less chaotic, smoke is blown into the hive. Although the basic procedure is the same, the conditions that the hunters work in are a lot more difficult. Besides the obvious risk of being stung by angry bees, the hunters must also be wary of being trampled to death by elephants. There is also the risk of injury involved in climbing up to get to the hives. A less serious problem with this style of honey hunting is that the hunters are often required to travel large distances and carry buckets weighed down with honey back to the village, which is not an easy task. The honey eaten in the Yao community is wildly different from the honey you buy at the grocery store, which has usually been collected from several different colonies mixed together and boiled down to become sweeter. The raw honey from the hives in Mozambique has a strong flavor that almost stings your throat. Raw honey draws its flavor from both the type of bees and the plants from which it is made to form a distinct taste. And there are hundreds of quite unique varieties of honey.

That is the end of Part 4. You now have 45 seconds to check your answers to Part 4.

analyses.content: 录音直接列举了雄鸟的特征，明确指出黄色的部分是 shoulder（肩部）斑块。
你可能会因为先听到黑色的“throat”而直接填入，但题目限定了是“yellow patch”，必须等录音说到黄色（yellow）后面的对应部位才行。
The male bird is recognizable by its pink beak, black throat, and yellow shoulder patch.
录音中描述幼鸟特征时，明确说它们眼睛周围有一圈显眼的 ring（环）。
题目要求填的是围绕着眼睛（surrounds the eye）的东西，你可能会填成前面刚提到的“throat”，但喉咙并不在眼睛周围。
The female has a black beak and a duller color, while the young birds have a distinctive yellow throat and a noticeable ring around the eye.
录音原词重现了“especially”，紧跟在它后面的 high（高）就是正确答案。
你可能会被后面补充说明的“hard”带偏，但题目考查的是与“especially”强绑定的形容词，必须严格对应。
The reason this relationship has developed is because the trees in the Niassa Reserve, therefore, the hives are especially high, sometimes up to thirty meters, which makes them very hard to find.
录音说明猎人拿走蜂蜜后会留下一些东西，而向蜜鸟能吃并消化 wax（蜂蜡）。
你可能没顺着逻辑往后听，顺手就填了“honey”，但蜂蜜是被猎人拿走的，鸟享受的实际上是剩下的蜂蜡。

The birds locate the beehives stashed away in holes in trees, which the hunters then access in order to make off with the pure, sticky honey inside. But they also leave something behind for the Greater Honeyguides. They are among the few bird species that can eat and digest wax in this way.
题目中的“importance”对应录音中的“role”（作用），录音明确指出这个作用变得 smaller（更小）。
你可能会在听到“farming”或“hives”时就急着作答，但题目问的是鸟的“重要性”发生了什么变化，需要抓取表示趋势的词。
But in some countries outside Mozambique, villagers are now turning more to farming and keeping their own hives, which has led to the role of the bird in honey collection growing smaller.
录音提到在赞比亚，砍伐 wood（木头）的声音是狩猎信号。
题干中的“being cut”（被砍）在录音中被替换成了“chopping”（砍伐），如果你没反应过来这两个词的同义替换，就会完全跟丢答案。
While in Zambia, the sound of chopping wood is the cue.
为了让蜜蜂放松，通常会往蜂巢里吹 smoke（烟）。
题目里的“soothe”（安抚）替换了录音里的“relax”（放松），如果你死等“soothe”这个词出现，就会错过前半句已经给出的动作主语。
In order to relax the bees and make the process less chaotic, smoke is blown into the hive.
录音指出除了被蜜蜂蛰，猎人还要小心被 elephants（大象）踩死。
题干的“killed by”替换了录音的“trampled to death by”，即使你不认识 trample，只要抓住“death by”也能准确识别出致死原因是大象。
Besides the obvious risk of being stung by angry bees, the hunters must also be wary of being trampled to death by elephants.
录音中提到猎人需要携带装满蜂蜜的 buckets（水桶）长途跋涉。
题目上的“heavy”被替换成了“weighed down with”（被...压得很重），如果你没听懂这个短语的意思，就容易错过它前面的名词。

A less serious problem with this style of honey hunting is that the hunters are often required to travel large distances and carry buckets weighed down with honey back to the village, which is not an easy task.
录音明确交代生蜂蜜的味道来自“both A and B”的结构，即蜜蜂的种类和 plants（植物）。
题干用“and”并列了两个来源，如果你只听到了前半个“bees”，就会漏掉后面由“both... and...”引出的第二个并列名词。
Raw honey draws its flavor from both the type of bees and the plants from which it is made to form a distinct taste.
